prompt: I put a ProximityPrompt inside a Folder in Workspace that holds my shop stand's parts, but no prompt ever appears when I walk up. Moving it into a different Model also didn't help, and on another stand the prompt only shows from some angles. What's wrong?
answer_key: A ProximityPrompt only works when parented to a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model that has its PrimaryPart set (in the Workspace); a Folder parent (or a Model without PrimaryPart) shows nothing

RequiresLineOfSight: when true the prompt is hidden if the path between the player's camera and the prompt's parent object is obstructed (the parent itself is excluded); set it false or move the prompt to an unobstructed part/Attachment
Check MaxActivationDistance: the character must be within that distance for the prompt to appear

responses.R1:
A ProximityPrompt only works when its parent is a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model that has a PrimaryPart set, and that parent must be in Workspace. A Folder is not a valid parent, so the prompt never appears. A Model without a PrimaryPart also fails, which is why moving it into another Model didn't help.
Fix: parent the prompt to an Attachment placed at the counter or handle, or to a BasePart, or set the Model's PrimaryPart.
The 'only from some angles' problem comes from RequiresLineOfSight, which defaults to true. Roblox checks for a clear line from the camera to the prompt's parent, so other parts of the stand block it from some sides. Put the prompt on an Attachment on the visible front face, or set RequiresLineOfSight = false. Also check MaxActivationDistance (default 10 studs), Enabled, and that the parent isn't buried inside a large part.
Sources: ProximityPrompt - Engine Reference Card; Clickable and Interactive Parts.
responses.R2: A ProximityPrompt only works when its parent is a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model (it uses the PrimaryPart). A Folder has no position, so the prompt never shows. In a Model with no PrimaryPart it also has nothing to anchor to. Fix: parent it to a part (or an Attachment in a part) at the counter. If it only shows from some angles, RequiresLineOfSight (default true) is being blocked by the stand's own geometry or a hitbox. Set RequiresLineOfSight = false, or move the part/Attachment so it sits in front of the geometry. Also check: Enabled = true, MaxActivationDistance is large enough, the prompt's position is in front of the stand (raise UIOffset if needed), Style is Default (Custom style draws nothing unless you build the UI), ClickablePrompt, and that ProximityPromptService.Enabled is on and no script hides prompts.
responses.R3: A ProximityPrompt only shows when its parent is a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model with PrimaryPart set, and that parent must be in Workspace. A Folder is not a valid parent, so nothing renders. Moving it into a Model didn't help because that Model has no PrimaryPart. Set PrimaryPart, or better, parent the prompt to an Attachment on the counter or handle part. The 'some angles only' stand is RequiresLineOfSight, which defaults to true: the prompt hides when geometry, often the stand's own big part, blocks the line from the camera to the prompt's parent. Move the prompt to an Attachment sitting in front of the surface, or set RequiresLineOfSight = false. Also check MaxActivationDistance (default 10 studs), Enabled, and that the stand isn't streamed out. Re-check distance on the server in the Triggered handler. (Sources: ProximityPrompt - Engine Reference Card; Clickable and Interactive Parts)

grader_notes: Do not penalise or require exact default values (e.g. 10 studs); they were not verified for this key.

prompt: My custom sword-swing animation plays in Studio when I test alone, but in the live game (owned by my group) nothing plays. On my test place it plays but the arms look half-blended with walking. I load it from a LocalScript with Humanoid:LoadAnimation. What should I check?
answer_key: Animation asset ownership: for a group-owned experience the animation must be published under/owned by that group (select the group as Creator when publishing) or it won't load in the live game
AnimationTrack.Priority: set the track (or animation) to Action (or higher: Action2-4) so it overrides Movement/Idle/Core animations; same-priority tracks blend by weight
Load via the Animator (Humanoid.Animator:LoadAnimation) instead of the deprecated Humanoid:LoadAnimation; loading on the client's own character also loads it for the server, so it replicates

responses.R1: 1) Ownership: a live game only plays animations whose creator matches the experience's creator. Your game is group-owned, so an animation uploaded to your personal account won't play there. It works in your own test place and in Studio because you own it. Fix: re-upload or publish the animation under the group, or grant the experience on the asset's Permissions page, then use the new id. Studio-registered or local keyframe ids never work live. 2) Half-blending with walking is a priority problem. The track is at Core or Movement priority (or the same priority as the walk), so the walk's arm keyframes blend in. Set the animation's priority to Action (or Action2-4) in the editor or with track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action. Note that Core is the lowest priority even though its .Value is 1000, so compare enums, not .Value. 3) Humanoid:LoadAnimation is deprecated. Use humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator"):LoadAnimation(anim), with the Animator created by the server/default character, so the playback replicates. Load each track once and cache it. Don't read Length before the track has loaded. (Sources: Animation Asset Permissions and Groups; Playback, Priorities and Blending)
responses.R2: 1) Ownership. Animations only load in games owned by the same user/group that owns the animation asset. Re-upload (or publish) the animation under the group, or grant the group's experience permission, and use the new ID. In Studio, your own account's animations work, which is why it plays there. 2) Use Humanoid.Animator:LoadAnimation (Humanoid:LoadAnimation is deprecated). Load it from the client on the local character's Animator, which replicates. Wait for the Animator: char:WaitForChild('Humanoid'):WaitForChild('Animator'). Cache the track instead of reloading it on every swing. 3) Half-blending: set track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action (or Action2-4) so it overrides Walk/Run/Idle, or set Priority on the asset in the Animation Editor before export. Also make sure the animation keys every arm joint you want overridden, because unkeyed joints keep playing the walk. Check that the weight is 1 (track:Play(0.1, 1, 1)). Make sure the rig type (R6 vs R15) matches the animation.
responses.R3:
1) Ownership (nothing plays live): the animation asset must be owned by the same creator as the experience. For a group game, publish or re-upload the animation under the group (set Creator to the group), or grant the experience permission on the asset in Creator Dashboard. A Studio solo test can load your personal animations; live servers can't. To diagnose, check the Output for a load or permission error, or see whether track.Length stays 0.
2) Half-blended with walking: this is a priority problem. A track left at Core (or Idle/Movement) blends with the default walk. Set the animation's Priority to Action (or Action2-4) in the editor or with track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action. Rank: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2-4. Don't compare by .Value, because Core = 1000.
3) Humanoid:LoadAnimation is deprecated. Use humanoid:FindFirstChildOfClass('Animator'):LoadAnimation(anim). The Animator should be created by the server (the default character already has one). Loading it from the client's own character is fine and replicates.
4) Load each track once and cache it. Every LoadAnimation call makes a new track, and there is a limit of about 256 tracks.
Sources: Publishing Animations; Playback, Priorities and Blending; Animator Deep Dive.

grader_notes: Item 3: saying Humanoid:LoadAnimation still works but is superseded by Animator earns full; recommending only Humanoid:LoadAnimation earns 0.5, not -1.

prompt: My shop ScrollingFrame uses a UIListLayout. I set each item's LayoutOrder to its price (10, 50, 200, 1000) but the list shows them in alphabetical order. Another dev says two items with equal LayoutOrder 'swap randomly'. Explain both.
answer_key: UIListLayout.SortOrder is set to Name, which sorts children alphanumerically by name and ignores LayoutOrder; set SortOrder to Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder
With SortOrder.LayoutOrder, children are sorted ascending by LayoutOrder (lower value first)
Ties are not random: children with the same LayoutOrder are ordered by which was added to the parent first

responses.R1:
1) LayoutOrder is only used when the UIListLayout's SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder. Your layout is set to SortOrder = Name, so it sorts the children alphabetically by Instance.Name and ignores LayoutOrder. Fix: layout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder. Then 10, 50, 200, 1000 sort ascending, smallest first. Gapped values like these make it easy to insert items later.
2) Equal LayoutOrder: ties have no stable, guaranteed order. Siblings with the same LayoutOrder can come out in a different order between sessions or after re-parenting or renaming, so they appear to 'swap'. Give every item a unique LayoutOrder, for example price*10 + index, or break ties by encoding a second key.
Also: SortOrder = Name re-sorts when items are renamed. Only direct children with a GuiObject are laid out.
Source: UI Layout Objects - Lists, Grids and Pages.
responses.R2: LayoutOrder is only used when UIListLayout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder. The default for older layouts, or one set to Name, sorts alphabetically by Name, so set SortOrder to LayoutOrder. LayoutOrder is an integer, so prices fit. Ties: when two siblings have the same LayoutOrder, the order is not defined by a secondary key you control. It depends on internal child order, which can change when instances are re-parented, cloned or replicated, so they can appear to swap. Fix: give each item a unique LayoutOrder, for example price*10 + index, or break ties by encoding a secondary key.
responses.R3: UIListLayout.SortOrder defaults to Enum.SortOrder.Name, so LayoutOrder is ignored and the children sort alphabetically by Name. Set layout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder and your 10/50/200/1000 values take effect (lower comes first). Equal LayoutOrder: the engine doesn't define a stable tie-break, so items with the same value can come out in a different order between sessions or after re-parenting or renaming. That is the 'random swap'. Fix: give every item a unique LayoutOrder, e.g. price*10 + index, or gapped values like 10, 20, 30. Always set SortOrder explicitly. Under Name sorting, renaming a child also reorders the menu. (Source: UI Layout Objects - Lists Grids and Pages)

prompt: Write a minimal server-side Luau handler that grants 100 coins when a player buys developer product 123456, and list the key rules so purchases are never lost or double-granted.
answer_key: Set MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt once, in a single server Script, handling all products (or use the newer MarketplaceService:BindReceiptHandler)

Return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted only after the benefit is actually granted/saved; return NotProcessedYet if the player isn't in the server or granting/saving fails, so the receipt is redelivered (e.g. when the player rejoins)
Make it idempotent: record receiptInfo.PurchaseId (e.g. in a DataStore) and skip re-granting a PurchaseId already processed
Look up the player via receiptInfo.PlayerId and the product via receiptInfo.ProductId

responses.R1:
```lua
-- ServerScriptService, the ONLY ProcessReceipt in the game
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Data = require(script.Parent.PlayerData) -- session-locked profile store
local PRODUCTS = { [123456] = function(profile) profile.Coins += 100 end }

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local profile = Data.get(player)
  local grant = PRODUCTS[info.ProductId]
  if not profile or not grant then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  if profile.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted end
  grant(profile)
  profile.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time()
  local ok = Data.saveNow(player) -- pcall'd save of the same document
  if not ok then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
Rules:
- Have exactly one ProcessReceipt. A second assignment silently replaces the first.
- Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved. On any failure, or if the player is absent, return NotProcessedYet; Roblox retries on their next join or purchase.
- Make it idempotent: store processed PurchaseIds in the same profile and the same save as the coins (not in a separate store).
- Never grant from PromptProductPurchaseFinished or from client remotes.
- Don't error or yield indefinitely inside the callback, and trim old receipt ids.
Source: Developer Products and ProcessReceipt.
responses.R2:
local MPS = game:GetService('MarketplaceService')
local DSS = game:GetService('DataStoreService')
local receipts = DSS:GetDataStore('PurchaseHistory')
local PRODUCT = 123456

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local player = game.Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  if info.ProductId ~= PRODUCT then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local key = info.PlayerId .. '_' .. info.PurchaseId
  local ok, err = pcall(function()
    receipts:UpdateAsync(key, function(done)
      if done then return nil end -- already granted
      addCoins(player, 100) -- your data module; must be saved/persisted
      return true
    end)
  end)
  if not ok then warn(err) return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end

Rules: set ProcessReceipt exactly once, in one server Script. Never grant from the client or from PromptProductPurchaseFinished. Make it idempotent by PurchaseId. Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved. Otherwise return NotProcessedYet and Roblox retries. Never yield forever or error. pcall DataStore calls. Handle the player having left. Ideally the session-locked profile records PurchaseIds and is saved before you return.
responses.R3:
-- ServerScriptService (the ONLY script that sets ProcessReceipt)
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Data = require(script.Parent.PlayerData) -- your session-locked profile store

local grants = {
  [123456] = function(profile) profile.Coins += 100 end,
}

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  local profile = player and Data.get(player)
  local grant = grants[info.ProductId]
  if not (profile and grant) then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  if profile.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted end
  grant(profile)                             -- no yield between grant and marker
  profile.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = true
  local ok = Data.saveNow(player)            -- pcall'd save
  if not ok then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end

Rules:
- Assign ProcessReceipt in exactly one server script.
- Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant has been saved. Otherwise return NotProcessedYet, and Roblox redelivers the receipt (e.g. when the player rejoins).
- Idempotency: store the PurchaseId in the same data document as the coins, so a retry can't double-grant.
- Return NotProcessedYet if the player has left, the product is unknown, or the save failed.
- Never grant from PromptProductPurchaseFinished or client remotes.
- Don't yield inside the grant function.
- Keep handlers for retired products.

grader_notes: BindReceiptHandler returning Enum.ReceiptDecision.Processed / NotProcessedYet is equally correct. Granting in PromptProductPurchaseFinished instead of a receipt handler: -1 on item 1.

prompt: Write a LocalScript that makes the player sprint (WalkSpeed 24, back to 16) while holding LeftShift on keyboard or ButtonL3 on gamepad, with an on-screen button on mobile, using ContextActionService. Note the key rules.
answer_key: ContextActionService:BindAction(actionName, handler, true, Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3) - the third argument (createTouchButton) creates the mobile touch button
Handler receives (actionName, inputState, inputObject); set speed on Enum.UserInputState.Begin and reset on End (and Cancel)
Return value: nil or Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink sinks the input; Enum.ContextActionResult.Pass lets the next bound action receive it; call UnbindAction when the context ends

responses.R1:
```lua
-- StarterPlayerScripts/Sprint (LocalScript)
local CAS = game:GetService("ContextActionService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local WALK, RUN = 16, 24

local function getHum()
  local c = player.Character
  return c and c:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
end

local function onSprint(_, state, _)
  local hum = getHum()
  if not hum then return Enum.ContextActionResult.Pass end
  if state == Enum.UserInputState.Begin then
    hum.WalkSpeed = RUN
  elseif state == Enum.UserInputState.End or state == Enum.UserInputState.Cancel then
    hum.WalkSpeed = WALK
  end
  return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink
end

CAS:BindAction("Sprint", onSprint, true, Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3)
CAS:SetTitle("Sprint", "Run")
CAS:SetPosition("Sprint", UDim2.new(1, -170, 1, -90))
player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function() local h = getHum() if h then h.WalkSpeed = WALK end end)
```
Rules:
- CAS runs client-side only. createTouchButton = true makes the button, which appears only on touch devices (GetButton returns nil elsewhere).
- Handle Begin, End and Cancel. Cancel fires when the binding is replaced or unbound, so reset the speed there.
- Return Sink to consume the input or Pass to let it through.
- Name actions by intent, and UnbindAction when the context ends.
- WalkSpeed set on the client replicates (the client owns its character), so the server should sanity-check speed.
- CAS BindAction is slated for deprecation in favor of the Input Action System.
responses.R2:
local CAS = game:GetService('ContextActionService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

local function setSpeed(s)
  local hum = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if hum then hum.WalkSpeed = s end
end

local function sprint(_, state, _)
  if state == Enum.UserInputState.Begin then setSpeed(24)
  elseif state == Enum.UserInputState.End or state == Enum.UserInputState.Cancel then setSpeed(16) end
  return Enum.ContextActionResult.Pass
end

CAS:BindAction('Sprint', sprint, true, Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3)
CAS:SetTitle('Sprint', 'Run')
CAS:SetPosition('Sprint', UDim2.new(1, -150, 1, -150))
player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function() setSpeed(16) end)

Rules: put it in StarterPlayerScripts (or StarterCharacterScripts). The third argument true creates the touch button, which is shown only on touch devices. Handle End and Cancel, since Cancel fires when focus is lost or the action is unbound, so you never get stuck sprinting. Return Pass or Sink as appropriate. Unbind with CAS:UnbindAction when needed. WalkSpeed set on the client replicates for your own character, so the server should validate speed for anti-cheat.
responses.R3:
-- StarterPlayerScripts LocalScript
local CAS = game:GetService("ContextActionService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

local function setSpeed(s)
  local hum = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if hum then hum.WalkSpeed = s end
end

local function onSprint(_, state, _)
  if state == Enum.UserInputState.Begin then setSpeed(24)
  elseif state == Enum.UserInputState.End or state == Enum.UserInputState.Cancel then setSpeed(16) end
  return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink
end

CAS:BindAction("Sprint", onSprint, true, Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3)
CAS:SetTitle("Sprint", "Run")
CAS:SetPosition("Sprint", UDim2.new(1, -150, 1, -150))
player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function() setSpeed(16) end)

Key rules:
- The handler gets (actionName, UserInputState, InputObject). React to Begin and End, and treat Cancel as release: Cancel fires when the binding is replaced or unbound.
- Return Sink to consume the input or Pass to let lower bindings see it. Returning nil also sinks.
- The third argument true creates the touch button, but only on touch devices. GetButton returns nil elsewhere.
- The newest binding wins unless you use BindActionAtPriority. BindAction is slated for deprecation in favour of the Input Action System.
- Name actions by intent ("Sprint"), and UnbindAction when the action no longer applies.
- Client-set WalkSpeed replicates through physics, so the server should cap speed if it matters.

grader_notes: Setting WalkSpeed from a LocalScript on the own character is acceptable here.

prompt: Write Luau that makes a door (hinged with a HingeConstraint between the frame and the door) swing open to 90 degrees and closed again, using the physics constraint rather than tweening the CFrame. Which properties matter?
answer_key: Set HingeConstraint.ActuatorType = Enum.ActuatorType.Servo
Drive it with TargetAngle, measured in degrees (90 to open, 0 to close)
Set ServoMaxTorque high enough to move the door and AngularSpeed for the swing speed (both apply with Servo); the door part must be unanchored

responses.R1:
-- Server Script. Door is unanchored; the frame is anchored.
local hinge = workspace.Door.HingeConstraint -- Attachment0 on frame, Attachment1 on door; both attachments' primary (X) axis = hinge axis
local door = workspace.Door.Panel

hinge.ActuatorType = Enum.ActuatorType.Servo
hinge.AngularSpeed = 2          -- rad/s swing rate
hinge.ServoMaxTorque = 1e5      -- must beat door inertia + friction
hinge.LimitsEnabled = true
hinge.LowerAngle, hinge.UpperAngle = -1, 91
door:SetNetworkOwner(nil)       -- server-owned so it doesn't jitter

local open = false
local function toggle()
  open = not open
  hinge.TargetAngle = open and 90 or 0 -- degrees
end
workspace.Door.Prompt.ProximityPrompt.Triggered:Connect(toggle)

Properties that matter:
- ActuatorType = Servo. Motor spins continuously; None swings freely.
- TargetAngle is in degrees, measured relative to the attachments' rest orientation.
- AngularSpeed sets how fast it swings. ServoMaxTorque too low means it sags or stalls; too high means it shoves players.
- LimitsEnabled with LowerAngle/UpperAngle are hard stops. Optional Restitution.
- Attachment0/Attachment1 must both be set and parented, or the constraint silently does nothing. Their X axes define the hinge axis, so check them visually with Show Constraint Details.
- The door must be unanchored and not welded to the frame. Keep its mass reasonable, or set Massless on decorations.
- Network ownership: SetNetworkOwner(nil) keeps it server-owned.
responses.R2:
local hinge = door.HingeConstraint -- Attachment0 on frame, Attachment1 on door; the hinge axis is the attachments' X axis (point it vertically)
hinge.ActuatorType = Enum.ActuatorType.Servo
hinge.LimitsEnabled = true
hinge.LowerAngle = 0
hinge.UpperAngle = 90
hinge.AngularSpeed = 2 -- rad/s
hinge.ServoMaxTorque = 1e6

local open = false
prompt.Triggered:Connect(function()
  open = not open
  hinge.TargetAngle = open and 90 or 0
end)

The properties that matter: ActuatorType = Servo, which drives to TargetAngle in degrees. AngularSpeed sets the swing speed, and ServoMaxTorque must be high enough to move the door's mass. AngularResponsiveness also matters for stiffness. Turn on LimitsEnabled with LowerAngle/UpperAngle (and Restitution) to clamp the swing. Attachment orientation sets the axis, so the attachment's primary axis must be vertical at the hinge edge. The door must be unanchored. The frame should be anchored. The door should not collide with the frame (use a NoCollisionConstraint or collision groups). For server-authoritative motion, keep network ownership on the server: door:SetNetworkOwner(nil). Use a light part or Massless pieces so the torque suffices.
responses.R3:
```lua
-- Server Script. Frame is Anchored; Door is unanchored (not welded to the frame).
local hinge = workspace.DoorModel.HingeConstraint -- Attachment0 on Frame, Attachment1 on Door
hinge.ActuatorType = Enum.ActuatorType.Servo
hinge.AngularSpeed = math.rad(90) -- radians/sec: about 1 s to swing
hinge.ServoMaxTorque = 1e6 -- enough to beat door mass and friction
hinge.LimitsEnabled = true
hinge.LowerAngle, hinge.UpperAngle = 0, 90 -- degrees
workspace.DoorModel.Door:SetNetworkOwner(nil) -- server-owned, so exploiters can't fling it

local open = false
local function setOpen(v)
  open = v
  hinge.TargetAngle = v and 90 or 0 -- degrees
end
workspace.DoorModel.Door.ProximityPrompt.Triggered:Connect(function() setOpen(not open) end)
```
Properties that matter:
- ActuatorType Servo (Motor just spins), TargetAngle in degrees, AngularSpeed (rad/s), ServoMaxTorque (too low means the door sags or stalls).
- LimitsEnabled with LowerAngle and UpperAngle as hard stops.
- Both attachments' primary axis (X) must point along the hinge line (vertical): rotate the attachments so their axes align.
- Only the frame is anchored. The door must be unanchored and not welded to the frame, and anything welded to the door moves with it.
- Keep the door server-owned (SetNetworkOwner(nil)). A client-owned door can be desynced.
Source: Physics Assemblies and Constraints; Network Ownership.

grader_notes: Stating TargetAngle is in radians (math.rad(90)) is -1 on item 2.

prompt: I want an admin command that shows a global announcement banner in every running server of my experience at once. How should I architect it, and what limits should I respect?
answer_key: Use MessagingService: every server SubscribeAsync to a topic at startup; the issuing server calls PublishAsync(topic, message); subscribers fire a RemoteEvent (FireAllClients) to show the banner
Delivery is best-effort and not guaranteed (typically within 1-2 s); wrap PublishAsync/SubscribeAsync in pcall and don't rely on it for critical state
Message size limit is 1 kB and topic names are 1-80 characters; there are per-server send and per-topic receive rate limits
Validate admin rights on the server before publishing (never trust the client's request)

responses.R1: Use MessagingService. An admin client fires a RemoteEvent with the text. The server verifies the sender is an admin (a UserId or group-rank check on the server, never trusting the client), rate-limits, filters the text with TextService:FilterStringAsync and GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync, then calls MessagingService:PublishAsync('Announce', {text=..., id=..., t=os.time()}) inside a pcall with retry. Every server calls SubscribeAsync('Announce', fn) at startup (in a pcall). The handler fires a RemoteEvent with FireAllClients to show the banner. The publishing server also receives its own message, so don't show it twice. Limits: the message payload is about 1 KB. Publish throughput is about 150 + 60*players per minute per server, and subscriptions are limited per server. Delivery is best-effort with no guarantee and no ordering, typically under a second. Delivery is not persisted, so servers started later miss it. For a 'current announcement' that new servers need, also store it in a DataStore or MemoryStore with an expiry and read it on startup. Dedupe by id. Keep topic names short. It does not work across experiences.
responses.R2:
Architecture:
- The admin runs a command (chat command or admin UI firing a RemoteEvent) on their server. That server authenticates them against a server-side admin list (UserIds or group rank). Never trust a client flag.
- The server validates and filters the text with TextService:FilterStringAsync / GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync, then calls MessagingService:PublishAsync("Announce", {id=..., text=..., expires=...}) inside pcall with retry.
- Every server runs SubscribeAsync("Announce", ...) at startup. On receipt it dedupes by id (the sender receives its own message too) and fires a RemoteEvent:FireAllClients to show the banner.
- For persistence or late joiners, write the current announcement to a DataStore or MemoryStore, and use the message as a 'go look' nudge.

Limits (MessagingService):
- Message payload: 1 KB. Topic name: up to 80 chars.
- Publishes per server: 600 + 240 x players per minute.
- Receives per topic: 40 + 80 x servers per minute. Experience-wide: 400 + 200 x servers per minute.
- Subscriptions per server: 20 + 8 x players.
- Delivery is best-effort (typically 1-2 s), with no ordering or delivery guarantee. Clocks differ between servers, so don't order by sender timestamps.
- Rate-limit the admin command. Open Cloud publishMessage can also trigger it from outside the game and shares the same limits.
(Sources: Cross-Server Messaging; MessagingService - Engine Reference Card)
responses.R3:
Architecture:
1) Admin UI or chat command -> RemoteEvent -> server. The server verifies the sender with a server-side allowlist (UserId or group rank) and never trusts the client. Rate-limit the command.
2) Filter the text with TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, userId), then GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync().
3) In task.spawn, call pcall(MessagingService.PublishAsync, MessagingService, "Announce", {text=..., id=..., t=os.time()}). Don't block the remote handler.
4) Every server calls MessagingService:SubscribeAsync("Announce", function(msg) ... end) once at startup, inside pcall with retry. It then does RemoteEvent:FireAllClients(msg.Data) and the clients show the banner. Dedupe by id and drop stale messages using msg.Sent.
Limits (Roblox docs, subject to change):
- Payload is 1 kB max.
- Sends per server: 600 + 240 x players per minute.
- Receives per topic: 40 + 80 x servers per minute. Receives for the whole experience: 400 + 200 x servers per minute.
- Subscriptions per server: 20 + 8 x players. Subscribe requests: 240/min per server.
- Delivery is best effort, typically 1-2 s, and not guaranteed or ordered. For a must-see message, also store it, e.g. in a MemoryStore or DataStore key that new servers read.
- Publish rarely; one topic suits low-frequency announcements. Studio behavior differs; test in live servers.
- Open Cloud publishMessage (an external admin panel) shares the same limits.
Source: MessagingService - Engine Reference Card; Cross-Server Messaging.

grader_notes: Exact rate formulas (600 + 240*players sends/min per server; 40 + 80*servers receives/min per topic) are not required; older figures (e.g. 150 + 60*players) earn 0.5 instead of -1.

prompt: I'm making a sword Tool that damages other players. How should I split the logic between client and server so it feels responsive but can't be exploited? Also, my Tool doesn't equip properly - it has a MeshPart called 'Blade' and no other parts.
answer_key: Client: detect use (Tool.Activated) and play animation/effects locally; send a RemoteEvent request without trusted damage values
Server: validate everything (tool equipped in the character, cooldown, target distance / hit check done or sanity-checked on the server) and apply damage server-side
Tools need a BasePart named 'Handle' unless Tool.RequiresHandle is false; rename the part to Handle or set RequiresHandle = false

responses.R1:
Split:
- Client (LocalScript in the tool or in PlayerScripts): on Activated, play the swing animation and sound right away for feel, and optionally show predicted hit effects. Then FireServer("Swing") with intent only. Never send the target or the damage.
- Server: rate-limit the remote and enforce the cooldown, with about 50-80 ms tolerance for latency. Check that the player is alive and the tool is equipped. Run the hitbox itself during the swing window with workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox/GetPartsInPart (not client Touched) in front of the player's root. Validate distance and line of sight with a raycast. Dedupe hits per swing per character, skip the attacker and teammates, then call Humanoid:TakeDamage on the server. Keep damage values server-side and the scripts in ServerScriptService.

Equip problem: Tool.RequiresHandle defaults to true, so the Tool needs a BasePart named exactly "Handle" as a direct child. With only a MeshPart called "Blade", it can't be held, and Equipped/Unequipped don't behave. Fix: rename Blade to Handle (and adjust Tool.Grip/GripPos), or add a small invisible Handle part welded to Blade. Alternatively, set RequiresHandle = false and weld the blade yourself. Make sure ManualActivationOnly is false so clicks fire Activated. (Sources: Tools and Inventory Systems; Melee Combat System End to End)
responses.R2: Client: play the swing animation and sound immediately, with optional local hit VFX for feel. Fire a RemoteEvent ('Swing'), or let the server detect hits on its own. Server: own all damage. On Swing, check the tool is equipped by that player, the character is alive, and the cooldown (server-side timestamp per player). Do the hit detection on the server (GetPartBoundsInBox / a Shapecast / spatial query in front of the HumanoidRootPart, or Touched on the blade during an active window), or validate a client-reported target. The target must be within range (distance plus ping slack), alive, not on the same team, and hit at most once per swing. Apply Humanoid:TakeDamage on the server. Never accept a damage amount from the client. Equip issue: by default Tool.RequiresHandle = true, so it needs a part named exactly 'Handle'. Rename 'Blade' to 'Handle' (or add a Handle part and weld the Blade to it with a WeldConstraint). Make it unanchored with CanCollide off, and adjust the grip with Tool.Grip / GripPos. Otherwise set RequiresHandle = false.
responses.R3:
Split:
- Client does feel only: plays the swing animation, sound and VFX immediately on Tool.Activated. It fires a RemoteEvent saying 'swing' and nothing else: no target, no damage.
- Server is the authority:
  - Rate-limit the remote and enforce the swing cooldown, with about 50-80 ms tolerance for latency.
  - Check the player is alive and the tool is equipped.
  - After the windup, re-check state and do its own hit query, e.g. workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox in front of the HumanoidRootPart or a short raycast.
  - Dedupe hits per model and check distance and line of sight.
  - Apply Humanoid:TakeDamage (this respects ForceFields).
- Never take damage or targets from client args, and don't rely on the client's Touched. The client may optionally send a hit hint that the server validates by distance.
Equip problem: Tool.RequiresHandle defaults to true and needs a BasePart child named exactly 'Handle'. With only 'Blade', the tool won't equip or Equipped won't fire. Rename the MeshPart to 'Handle' and adjust GripPos/Grip. Alternatively, add a small Handle part welded to Blade, or set RequiresHandle = false and attach it yourself. Make sure Handle is unanchored and CanCollide is usually false. Also check ManualActivationOnly is false, or Activated won't fire from clicks.
Sources: Tools and Inventory Systems; Melee Combat System End to End.

prompt: I replicate each player's aim direction to all other clients 30 times a second with a RemoteEvent and see network lag. Someone suggested UnreliableRemoteEvent. When is it appropriate, and what are its constraints?
answer_key: UnreliableRemoteEvent is unordered and unreliable: lost events are not resent and don't wait for earlier ones - suited to ephemeral/continuously changing data like aim; use RemoteEvent where order or reliability matters
Payloads larger than 1000 bytes are dropped
Client-to-server remotes are throttled at roughly 500 requests per second per client, shared among all remotes of the same type; lower the send rate / batch

responses.R1: UnreliableRemoteEvent suits frequent, ephemeral, superseded data where a lost or out-of-order packet doesn't matter because the next update replaces it: aim direction, cursor, cosmetic look-at, VFX triggers. Constraints: delivery is not guaranteed and ordering is not guaranteed. The payload is limited (about 1000 bytes per call). Larger payloads are dropped, not sent. There's no ack. Don't use it for game-critical events (damage, purchases, state changes) or one-off events. It uses the same API (FireServer/FireAllClients/OnClientEvent) and the same security rules (validate and rate-limit on the server). Also reduce the cost: send compact data (a quantized yaw/pitch number instead of a CFrame), send only when it changed beyond a threshold, use a lower rate (10-20 Hz), and interpolate on receivers. Batch players into one server broadcast per tick instead of relaying each one. Consider skipping players far away.
responses.R2:
UnreliableRemoteEvent fits high-frequency, transient, superseded-by-the-next-update data, like your aim direction: losing one packet doesn't matter because the next one replaces it. It has its own pool, so it doesn't clog the reliable remotes used for hits and purchases.
Constraints:
- Delivery is best effort and unordered: messages can be dropped or arrive out of order. It doesn't yield, and there are no RemoteFunction-style returns.
- Payloads over about 1,000 bytes are dropped silently. Send a few numbers, not tables of instances; e.g. pack yaw/pitch, or quantize into a buffer.
- Rate is roughly 500 calls/s per client, shared across remotes of that type, and the excess is dropped.
- Never use it for state changes or one-off events (start/stop, damage, purchases). A lost 'stop' sticks. Use RemoteEvent for those.
Also:
- Cut the rate to 10-20 Hz and interpolate on receivers.
- Send only when the value changed beyond a threshold.
- On the server, validate and rate-limit the input, then relay server-built values. FireAllClients only to players who need it (or nearby ones), not raw client args.
Source: RemoteEvents, RemoteFunctions and Unreliable Remotes; Network Performance.
responses.R3:
UnreliableRemoteEvent is appropriate for high-frequency, replaceable state, where a lost packet is fixed by the next one: aim or look direction, cursor position, cosmetic positions. Your aim stream is the textbook case.

Constraints:
- Delivery can drop packets and arrive out of order. Add a small sequence number or timestamp and ignore stale updates.
- Payloads over about 1,000 bytes  are silently dropped, so keep messages tiny, e.g. a compressed Vector3 or two angles in a buffer.
- There's no return value or yielding (no Invoke) and no delivery confirmation.
- Calls above the rate budget (about 500 calls/s per client, per remote type) are dropped rather than queued. Reliable remotes have their own pool, so reliable traffic isn't starved.
- Never use it for state changes, purchases, damage, or the start or end of an ability. Those need RemoteEvent.

Also reduce the rate: send about 10-20 Hz, only when the aim changed beyond a threshold, and interpolate on receivers. The server should validate (types, finite values, unit vector) and rate-limit before relaying with FireAllClients/FireClient, skipping the sender. (Source: RemoteEvents RemoteFunctions and Unreliable Remotes)

grader_notes: Item 2: 900 bytes (an earlier figure) earns 0.5 instead of -1.

prompt: After enabling StreamingEnabled, my client script errors with 'attempt to index nil' when it reads workspace.Map.Castle.Gate, and a teleport pad drops players into a void for a second. How do I fix both?
answer_key: With instance streaming, distant parts may not exist on the client; use WaitForChild (with timeout) / ChildAdded / CollectionService signals and handle parts streaming out, instead of direct indexing

Set Model.ModelStreamingMode on important models: Atomic (model and descendants stream in/out together) or Persistent (sent soon after join, before Workspace.PersistentLoaded, not streamed out); PersistentPerPlayer also exists
Before moving the character, call Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(position) on the server so the destination is streamed in first

responses.R1:
1) Nil index: with StreamingEnabled, distant parts aren't on the client yet, so workspace.Map.Castle.Gate may not exist. Use WaitForChild down the chain, with a timeout and a nil check:
local gate = workspace:WaitForChild("Map"):WaitForChild("Castle", 10)
gate = gate and gate:WaitForChild("Gate", 10)
Set the Castle (or Gate) Model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic, so the whole model arrives at once and one wait is enough. Use Persistent only for small essentials that every client must always have; it costs memory for every player. Better still, tag interactables with CollectionService and handle them through GetInstanceAddedSignal and the removed signal, since parts can also stream out again. Don't fix this by turning streaming off.

2) Void at teleport: the destination isn't streamed in when the character arrives. On the server, before moving the character, call player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(targetPosition, 5) inside a pcall (it yields), then do character:PivotTo(targetCFrame). Optionally anchor the HumanoidRootPart briefly, or keep a persistent landing floor. Player.ReplicationFocus only changes the streaming focus point; it doesn't replace the request. (Source: Instance Streaming)
responses.R2: 1) With streaming, parts far from the player may not exist on the client yet. Use workspace:WaitForChild('Map'):WaitForChild('Castle'):WaitForChild('Gate') (with a timeout), or listen with ChildAdded / CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal and handle removal (streaming out). Mark the Castle model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic so it streams as a unit, or Persistent/PersistentPerPlayer if the client must always have it. Never assume a streamed instance stays. 2) Teleport void: the destination area isn't streamed in when you move the character. On the server, call player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(targetPosition, timeout) before setting the character CFrame (pivot), or on the client before moving. Also consider anchoring the HumanoidRootPart briefly until the floor exists. Tune StreamingMinRadius / StreamingTargetRadius. Use StreamingIntegrityMode (PauseOutsideLoadedArea) so the player is paused rather than falling.
responses.R3:
1) Nil index: with StreamingEnabled, parts far away (or not yet arrived) don't exist on the client, so workspace.Map.Castle.Gate can be nil.
- Use WaitForChild down the chain, with timeouts: local gate = workspace:WaitForChild('Map'):WaitForChild('Castle', 10) and so on, then handle nil.
- Or tag the gate and use CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal plus GetTagged, so it also handles stream-out and stream-in.
- Set the Castle model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic so it arrives whole. Use Persistent only for the few models the client must always have.
- Code must also tolerate the gate streaming out again.
2) Void on teleport: the destination hasn't streamed in yet, so the player falls through. On the server, before moving them, call pcall(player.RequestStreamAroundAsync, player, targetPos, 5). Then check the player and character still exist and do character:PivotTo(CFrame.new(targetPos)).
- Optionally anchor the HumanoidRootPart briefly, or keep a Persistent landing platform.
- Defaults: StreamingMinRadius 64, StreamingTargetRadius 1024. Prefer StreamOutBehavior Opportunistic and ModelStreamingBehavior Improved.
- Don't disable streaming to hide the bug.
Source: Instance Streaming.

prompt: In late 2025 Roblox changed how Luau type checking works in Studio. What changed, and how do I turn the new type solver on for a project that uses --!strict?
answer_key: Luau's New Type Solver reached general release (announced Nov 20, 2025), moving out of Studio Beta; the Studio Beta toggle was removed on Jan 7, 2026
Scripts using nocheck/nonstrict modes moved to the new solver automatically; projects with strict scripts stay on the old solver by default
Opt in via the Workspace property UseNewLuauTypeSolver = Enabled (Scripting category); nonstrict became the default typecheck mode (LuauTypeCheckMode)

responses.R1: Roblox moved Luau to the new type solver in Studio. It's a rewrite of type inference with better refinement and generics, user-defined type functions, and fewer false positives. It became the default for --!nocheck and --!nonstrict scripts (non-strict is the default mode). The Studio Beta toggle for the new solver was scheduled for removal on January 7, 2026. Strict-mode scripts were not switched automatically. To use the new solver in a --!strict project, set the UseNewLuauTypeSolver setting from Default to Enabled; the docs doesn't say exactly where that setting lives in Studio today. Expect a wave of new or different errors on large strict codebases. Remove old-solver workarounds (casts through any, redundant annotations), and keep treating remote arguments as unknown and narrowing them at runtime, because types don't validate network input. (Sources: Engine and API Changes 2025-2026; Luau Type System and Strict Mode. The 'late 2025' timing is unverified.)
responses.R2: Roblox shipped Luau's new type solver (a rewrite of the type inference engine) out of beta in Studio. It was previously opt-in via the Beta Features 'New Luau type solver'. Changes: better inference (generalization, type functions such as keyof/index/user-defined 'type function's, read-only properties, improved refinements and unions/intersections, fewer false positives). Script Analysis and autocomplete use it. --!strict, --!nonstrict and --!nocheck mode comments still work the same way; the solver choice is a separate setting. To enable it: in Studio, File > Beta Features (or Studio Settings > Script Editor/Luau, depending on version) enable 'New Luau Type Solver' and restart Studio. It then applies to all scripts, including --!strict ones. Outside Studio (luau-lsp / luau-analyze), enable the new solver flag (e.g. luau-lsp 'luau-lsp.fflags.enableNewSolver' / FFlag LuauSolverV2=true). Expect some new errors in strict code. Fix annotations rather than downgrading to nonstrict.
responses.R3:
Luau's New Type Solver (a rewrite of type inference) reached general release in November 2025. Notes flag the exact date as partly unverified.
What changed:
- It became the default for non-strict scripts. Strict-mode (--!strict) projects were not migrated automatically.
- The Studio Beta Features toggle was removed (on 7 Jan 2026). Control is now a per-place setting.
- The new solver gives more accurate inference and enables new features: user-defined type functions, read/write property modifiers, and better keyof/index and refinements. It also reports new or different errors.
How to turn it on for a --!strict project:
- In Studio, select Workspace and set the UseNewLuauTypeSolver property (RolloutState) to Enabled. Default follows Roblox's rollout and Disabled opts out.
- Keep --!strict at the top of files. Workspace.LuauTypeCheckMode sets the mode for files without a directive.
- Expect a batch of new errors on a large strict codebase. Fix them on a branch, and make sure the whole team uses the same solver setting (same for external tooling like luau-lsp, which has its own new-solver flag).
Source: Luau Type System and Strict Mode; Engine and API Changes 2025-2026.

grader_notes: Item 1: 'November 2025' is enough. Saying it is still beta-only earns 0, not -1.

prompt: What is Roblox's Input Action System, which instances does it use, and how would I make a 'Jump' action that works from Space and from an on-screen button?
answer_key: Instances: InputContext (groups actions; Enabled/Priority/Sink), InputAction (a gameplay action that registers to its nearest ancestor InputContext), InputBinding (maps a hardware input to the action)
Create an InputAction with Type Bool and listen to InputAction.Pressed (false->true) / Released, or StateChanged
Use separate InputBindings for the key (KeyCode = Space) and the on-screen button (UIButton) - a single binding listens to only one input source
Status: Studio Beta in 2025, publishable via Client Beta from Aug 2025, announced fully released in June 2026

responses.R1:
The Input Action System (IAS) is Roblox's declarative, cross-device input system, fully released June 11, 2026. It is the successor to ContextActionService. Instances:
- InputContext: a group of actions. Properties: Enabled, Priority, Sink.
- InputAction: Type is Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D or ViewportPosition. Events: Pressed/Released (Bool only) and StateChanged. Methods: GetState(), Fire().
- InputBinding: KeyCode, UIButton, modifiers, thresholds, composite directions, Scale, ResponseCurve.

Jump example (LocalScript):
local ctx = Instance.new("InputContext")
ctx.Priority = 100; ctx.Sink = true
local jump = Instance.new("InputAction")
jump.Name = "Jump"; jump.Type = Enum.InputActionType.Bool; jump.Parent = ctx
local key = Instance.new("InputBinding"); key.KeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.Space; key.Parent = jump
local btn = Instance.new("InputBinding"); btn.UIButton = playerGui.HUD.JumpButton; btn.Parent = jump
ctx.Parent = player.PlayerGui
jump.Pressed:Connect(function()
  local h = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if h then h.Jump = true end
end)

Notes:
- Add a gamepad binding (ButtonA) too.
- The default character jump may also fire, so use Priority and Sink, or migrate the PlayerScripts. Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem is planned to become default-on in early 2027.
- Poll GetState() for continuous analog input.
responses.R2:
The Input Action System is Roblox's declarative, instance-based input layer, replacing much of ContextActionService/UserInputService binding code. Instances: InputContext (a group of actions with Enabled, Priority, Sink; put it under a player's PlayerGui/client), InputAction (one action with Type = Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D, ViewportPosition etc.; events Pressed, Released, StateChanged; GetState()), and InputBinding (a child of an InputAction mapping a source: KeyCode, a composite Up/Down/Left/Right for directions, or UIButton = a GuiButton for touch). Example (LocalScript):
local ctx = Instance.new('InputContext')
ctx.Parent = player.PlayerGui
local jump = Instance.new('InputAction')
jump.Name = 'Jump'; jump.Type = Enum.InputActionType.Bool; jump.Parent = ctx
local kb = Instance.new('InputBinding'); kb.KeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.Space; kb.Parent = jump
local btn = Instance.new('InputBinding'); btn.UIButton = screenGui.JumpButton; btn.Parent = jump
jump.Pressed:Connect(function()
  local hum = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if hum then hum.Jump = true end
end)
You can also build these in Explorer, without code. Use context Priority/Sink to override default controls.
responses.R3:
The Input Action System (IAS) is Roblox's newer, instance-based input-mapping system that supersedes ContextActionService. You declare actions and their bindings as instances instead of code.
Instances:
- InputContext: a group of actions, with Enabled, Priority and Sink. A higher-Priority context with Sink consumes its bound inputs from lower contexts.
- InputAction (child of a context): Type is Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D or ViewportPosition. Events are Pressed and Released (Bool only) and StateChanged; there's also GetState() and Fire().
- InputBinding (child of an action): KeyCode (or composite Up/Down/Left/Right keys, modifiers), and UIButton, which points at a GuiButton that drives the action on touch.
Jump example: put the instances in StarterGui (or under the PlayerGui), then:
```lua
local ctx = Instance.new("InputContext")
ctx.Parent = script
local jump = Instance.new("InputAction")
jump.Name = "Jump"
jump.Type = Enum.InputActionType.Bool
jump.Parent = ctx
local kb = Instance.new("InputBinding")
kb.KeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.Space
kb.Parent = jump
local btn = Instance.new("InputBinding")
btn.UIButton = script.Parent.JumpGui.JumpButton
btn.Parent = jump
jump.Pressed:Connect(function()
  local h = game.Players.LocalPlayer.Character and game.Players.LocalPlayer.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if h then h.Jump = true end
end)
```
Notes:
- You can add a gamepad binding, e.g. ButtonA.
- Default player scripts move to IAS via Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem (opt-in 2026, default planned early 2027).
- For analog actions, poll GetState(), because StateChanged won't fire while held steady.
Source: Input - UserInputService and ContextActionService; Server Authority and Input Migration 2026.

grader_notes: Item 4: accept either 'client beta' or 'fully released'; stating it is Studio-only/unpublishable earns 0.5. Item 3: one binding with both KeyCode and UIButton earns 0.5 (that worked before Feb 2026).
